summary: We developed a web application that helps identify safer and more efficient landing locations near the Moon’s South Pole. Using historical data on lunar rotation and surface activity, our platform tracks sunlight angles across specific craters to estimate how effectively a rover can charge its solar panels. It also analyses surface conditions to identify smoother, less rugged areas, helping make future lunar landings safer and more reliable.
details: Moon_Landers is a web-based lunar navigation platform designed to help researchers, scientists, and students identify the most suitable and efficient routes to reach the Moon’s South Pole. Our website uses historical lunar data from the past 10 years to analyse sunlight exposure, surface conditions, and important geographical features. Through an interactive 3D simulation built using Three.js, users can explore the Moon’s South Pole and its significant craters, understand sunlight availability, and identify potential landing zones. By analyse sunlight angles and surface characteristics, the platform helps locate safer landing areas while maximising solar energy availability for future lunar rovers and missions. The project is developed using HTML, Three.js, and Codex, combining web technologies and 3D visualisation to make lunar exploration planning more accessible, interactive, and efficient.
